title: GATP Seminar – Andrew Dancer (Oxford)
desc: Symplectic implosion is an abelianisation construction in symplectic geometry. The implosion of the cotangent bundle of a group K plays a universal role in the implosion of manifolds with a K-action. This universal implosion, which is usually a singular variety, can also be viewed as the non-reductive Geometric Invariant Theory quotient of the complexification G of K by its maximal unipotent subgroup. In this talk, we describe joint work with Johan Martens and Nick Proudfoot which uses point-counting techniques to calculate the intersection cohomology of the universal implosion.
venue: Huxley 658, Huxley Building, South Kensington Campus

title: SPC Seminar – Climate – Quran Wu (University of Reading)
desc:
Title: New Constraint on Future Ocean Heat Uptake Revealed by Considering Model Spread of Radiative Forcing

Speaker: Quran Wu (University of Reading)

Abstract: Human-induced climate change has resulted in a positive Earth energy imbalance at the top of the atmosphere. About 90% of this energy imbalance is taken up by the ocean. Ocean heat uptake (OHU) is therefore a key metric for assessing future climate risk. Contemporary climate models exhibit an intermodel spread in simulated OHU under a given future emissions scenario. Previous studies have investigated this spread in terms of ocean processes (e.g. OHU efficiency) and attempted to constrain it using historical OHU. However, the role of radiative forcing, the fundamental driver of OHU, has not been explicitly considered in previous…

title: Dynamical Systems Seminar – David Parmenter (University of Bristol)
desc:
Speaker : David Parmenter

Title : Cones on leaves: exponential convergence to the Margulis measure via an unstable transfer operator

Abstract : In this talk I’ll prove that for a uniformly hyperbolic diffeomorphism, the pull back of the leaf volume on a pushed forward piece of unstable manifold converges exponentially fast to the Margulis measure (the unstable measure of maximal entropy). In order to do this I’ll introduce notions of Birkhoff cones, transfer operators and prove an unstable analogue of the Ruelle-Perron-Frobenius theorem.

title: Finance and Stochastics Seminar – Martin Friesen
desc:
Speaker : Martin Friesen

Title : Boundary behavior of the Volterra square-root process

Abstract : The classical square-root diffusion, also known as the Cox-Ingersoll-Ross (CIR) process, admits a complete characterization of its boundary behavior through the well-known Feller condition. For its non-Markovian analogue, the rough or Volterra square-root process, the situation is considerably more subtle, as memory and roughness fundamentally alter the dynamics. In this talk, we review recent advances on the boundary behavior of Volterra square-root processes. For regular kernels, we present a natural analogue of the Feller condition that explicitly captures the effect of memory. In contrast, for singular kernels we show that the process necessarily hits the boundary. As an application,…

title: Universe Community Colloquium: Professor Chris Clarkson – Signatures of general relativity in galaxy clustering
desc:
Signatures of general relativity in galaxy clustering

Future galaxy surveys will map the large-scale structure of the Universe with unprecedented precision. One of their main goals is to use galaxy clustering to test the physics of the early Universe and search for primordial non-Gaussianity. On the largest scales, however, the observed galaxy distribution is not simply a three-dimensional density field: it is reconstructed from light arriving on our past lightcone, and is affected by a variety of relativistic projection effects and distortions. Alongside lensing and redshift-space distortions, a hierarchy of more subtle effects comes into play.
